text:
laura: heads-up — starting a canary for model-omega v2 in ~1h. we need a concrete automatic fallback chain defined before rollout. thinking: model-variant -> regional -> capacity -> degrade. any objections?

sam: +1 on a chain. can we be explicit about the triggers? e.g. latency p95 > 600ms or error_rate > 3% for 30s?

miguel: i'd add request queue-length and memory pressure as signals too. if GPU mem cross > 85% we should prefer var-quantized fallback.

priya: agree. also we need telemetry tags for fallback_reason so we can query fallback_rate by route + model variant. console dashboard should show per-split fallback_count and avg latency post-fallback.

laura: noted. spec draft below — lightweight JSON for the rollout policy we've been iterating on:

```
{
  "rollout": "canary",
  "traffic_split": {"v2": 10, "v1": 90},
  "fallback_chain": [
    {"type":"model_variant", "match":"compatible", "variants":["v1-quant","v1-fp16"], "triggers":{"p95_ms":600, "error_rate":0.03}},
    {"type":"regional_failover", "order":["same-region","nearest-healthy-region"], "triggers":{"instance_unavailable":true}},
    {"type":"capacity_redirect", "action":"reroute_to_dedicated_or_queue", "triggers":{"gpu_free_lt":1, "queue_latency_ms":200}},
    {"type":"degrade_to_smaller_model", "model":"small-llm", "max_quality_loss_pct":5}
  ],
  "safety": {"max_split_change_per_min":5, "circuit_breaker_window_s":60}
}
```

ellen: that looks sane. two UX points for the console: 1) allow visualizing the chain as a DAG with hoverable triggers, 2) expose a single toggle for "auto-fallback on" with an advanced editor for rules — most PMs want the toggle + presets.

sam: on implementation, we need to decide who owns the enforcement: router (edge) vs runtime. My preference: router should do quick regional/capacity checks and reroute; actual model_variant swap should be done by runtime to preserve KV cache semantics.

miguel: runtime swap is heavier (KV warm/cold). for model_variant fallback we should try variants with compatible KV layout first to avoid full cache wipe. add a compatibility tag and prefer compatible variants.

priya: telemetry hooks: emit metrics: fallback_attempts_total{route,reason}, fallback_success_total, fallback_latency_ms histogram, fallback_kv_warm=false/true tag. Also create an alert rule: fallback_rate > 1% sustained for 5m -> page on-call.

laura: agreed. also need billing note: when we fall back cross-region, cost may spike. ops wants a per-fallback_charge metric so finance can reconcile.

deploy-bot: canary rollout for model-omega v2 started (canary=10%) — runbooks: /runbooks/model-rollouts.

sam: edge cases: what if fallback loop occurs (region -> variant -> capacity -> region)? add a max_fallback_hops=2 per-request to avoid loops.

miguel: +1. also add a per-request header X-Fallback-Path we can surface in logs for debugging.

priya: UX: on the rollout config page show a small histogram preview that simulates impact of fallback rules given historical traffic (latency/error distributions). helps PMs pick thresholds.

laura: action items:
- miguel: add compatibility tags and max_hops enforcement in runtime (ETA EOD tomorrow)
- priy a: add telemetry metric names and update alert runbooks (ETA Friday)
- ellen: mockups for fallback DAG and simulation histogram (ETA Tue)
- sam: split enforcement doc: router vs runtime responsibilities (PR this week)

sam: quick question — should the default preset include "degrade_to_smaller_model" or keep that opt-in? i worry about quality regressions silently happening.

laura: keep degrade opt-in. it requires explicit risk sign-off and we should require an explicit "allow_degrade":true flag per-rollout.

priya: also require a canary-only flag for experimental degrade so it never hits prod without manual promote.

laura: cool. thanks everyone — i'll merge this draft into the rollout RFC and post a follow-up with console mocks. :thumbsup:

miguel: thanks. recording notes for post-mortem telemetry and perf baseline.

deploy-bot: canary health summary (5m): p95 420ms, errors 0.8%, fallbacks 2 -> monitoring OK so far.
